hero.purpose: The one thing a screen is fundamentally about — a name, a headline moment.

title.purpose: Card titles and weighted section headings.

metric.purpose: A single big standalone number (calories, weight). Not for multi-up rows.

overline.purpose: Eyebrows, field labels, step counters. Always uppercase.

shadows.name: card
shadows.purpose: Default shadow for Cards and inputs.

motion.name: duration-fast
motion.purpose: Default for taps; nothing on a tap should exceed this.

motion.name: duration-idle
motion.purpose: One full cycle of the mascot's idle breathing loop.

motion.name: curve-standard
motion.purpose: Default for anything already on screen moving or resizing.

motion.name: curve-entrance
motion.purpose: Things arriving: fast out of the gate, settling softly.

motion.name: spring-snappy
motion.purpose: The default 'chips and cells' bouncy press pattern — buttons, chips, cells.

motion.name: spring-celebrate
motion.purpose: Reward moments only — the mascot's celebration bounce. Pronounced overshoot; never for routine taps.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The main call-to-action fill, colored by the screen's domain (defaults to Rouge Baie).
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { background: #C2325A; color: #FFFFFF; font-family: 'Fredoka', sans-serif; font-weight: 700; font-size: 14px; line-height: 18px; letter-spacing: 0.1px; padding: 14px 16px; border-radius: 26px; border: none; box-shadow: 0 12px 26px rgba(163,28,66,0.28); background-image: linear-gradient(135deg, rgba(255,255,255,0.45) 0%, rgba(255,255,255,0) 55%, rgba(58,46,34,0.10) 100%); transition: transform 0.16s cubic-bezier(0.2,0,0,1), background-color 0.16s cubic-bezier(0.2,0,0,1); } .ds-btn-primary:hover { transform: translateY(-1px); } .ds-btn-primary:active { background: #A31C42; transform: scale(0.9); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #A31C42; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: Ghost/alternate action — ignores the screen's domain color entirely.
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { background: #FFFFFF; color: #2E2418; font-family: 'Fredoka', sans-serif; font-weight: 700; font-size: 14px; line-height: 18px; letter-spacing: 0.1px; padding: 14px 16px; border-radius: 26px; border: none; box-shadow: 0 12px 26px rgba(46,36,24,0.18); transition: transform 0.16s cubic-bezier(0.2,0,0,1), background-color 0.16s cubic-bezier(0.2,0,0,1); } .ds-btn-secondary:hover { transform: translateY(-1px); } .ds-btn-secondary:active { background: #FFF3E0; transform: scale(0.9); } .ds-btn-secondary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #2E2418; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Card
components.description: Default raised container — puffy sheen overlay, warm shadow, generous radius.
components.html: Contenu de la carte
components.css: .ds-card { position: relative; background: #FFFFFF; border-radius: 26px; padding: 12px; box-shadow: 0 8px 18px rgba(58,46,34,0.12); overflow: hidden; } .ds-card-sheen { position: absolute; inset: 0; border-radius: 26px; background: linear-gradient(135deg, rgba(255,255,255,0.45) 0%, rgba(255,255,255,0) 55%, rgba(58,46,34,0.10) 100%); pointer-events: none; } .ds-card-body { font-family: 'Fredoka', sans-serif; font-weight: 400; font-size: 14px; line-height: 21px; color: #2E2418; margin: 0; position: relative; }

components.name: Text Field
components.description: Labeled text input with a thickening-border focus state (padding compensates so the box doesn't jump).
components.css: .ds-field-label { display: block; font-family: 'Fredoka', sans-serif; font-weight: 700; font-size: 10px; line-height: 14px; letter-spacing: 1.2px; text-transform: uppercase; color: #6B5A46; margin-bottom: 4px; } .ds-field-input { width: 100%; box-sizing: border-box; font-family: 'Fredoka', sans-serif; font-weight: 400; font-size: 14px; line-height: 21px; color: #2E2418; background: #FFFFFF; border-radius: 16px; padding: 12px; border: 1px solid #F0D9B8; box-shadow: 0 8px 18px rgba(58,46,34,0.12); } .ds-field-input:focus { outline: none; border: 2px solid #C2325A; padding: 11px; }

components.name: Choice Pill (Selected)
components.description: A selected filter/day-tab pill, filled with the screen's domain color.
components.css: .ds-pill { font-family: 'Fredoka', sans-serif; font-weight: 600; font-size: 14px; line-height: 20px; padding: 10px 14px; border-radius: 28px; border: none; box-shadow: 0 8px 18px rgba(58,46,34,0.12); } .ds-pill-selected { background: #C2325A; color: #FFFFFF; box-shadow: 0 8px 18px rgba(194,50,90,0.25); }

narrative.overview:
FitFork's entire visual identity radiates from its mascot: a stylized cartoon broccoli character with big Pixar-style eyes and coral-orange sneakers, who lives permanently in the app and reacts to what the user does. Every other decision in this system exists to give that character a world it belongs in — puffy, warm-lit, hand-shaped surfaces instead of flat panels; four saturated domain colors instead of one cold brand accent; a single rounded typeface (Fredoka) that reads as friendly rather than clinical; and a deliberately bouncy, springy press feel on every tappable surface, because a claymorphic world should feel physically squishable, not just visually soft.

The interaction philosophy is ludique et rebondissant — playful and bouncy. The bounce is not a subtle acknowledgment of a tap; it is a visible, springy overshoot on release, present on buttons, chips, and cells alike. This is a deliberate reversal of the flat, restrained 'no bounce on a button' convention common to generic productivity apps — energy here comes from volume and motion, not from a loud palette or aggressive gradients.

This system explicitly rejects generic flat SaaS: thin-bordered flat cards, blue-violet gradients, and the interchangeable 'professional tool' look that could belong to any B2B dashboard. FitFork is a home-workout and home-cooking companion, not an enterprise tool — it should never look like one.
keyCharacteristics: One mascot, three poses (idle, celebrating, encouraging), permanently present rather than a decorative one-off
Four domain colors (nutrition, sport, progress, neutral) — no single brand accent
Puffy claymorphic volume: generous radii, two-tier warm shadows, a diagonal light-catching sheen on every raised surface
One rounded typeface (Fredoka) carrying everything from hero text to button labels
Deliberately bouncy, springy motion as the default interaction feel, not an occasional flourish
Light-only by tested decision, not by omission

rules.name: The One Domain Rule
rules.body: A screen that's fundamentally about nutrition uses Ambre Grillé for its accents; a sport screen uses Vert Forêt. Don't mix two domain colors as accents on the same screen without a specific reason.

rules.name: The Domain Vocabulary Never Remaps Rule
rules.body: Macro Protéine/Glucides/Lipides and Effort/Repos are fixed hues independent of screen domain — a recipe's protein number is always Macro Protéine-colored, even on a Vert Forêt sport screen.

rules.name: The Legacy Red Rule
rules.body: accentRed/accentRedDeep/accentRedSoft still exist in code as a transitional shim for screens not yet migrated to explicit domain tokens. Never reach for them in new or touched code — use the domain tokens directly.

rules.name: The One Family Rule
rules.body: Fredoka carries every text role in the app. Never introduce a second typeface, and always spread a whole typography.* role object so family, size, leading, and tracking travel together.

rules.name: The Puffy Sheen Rule
rules.body: Every raised surface gets a diagonal gradient overlay sized to fill it exactly, with a matching border radius and pointerEvents none. The parent surface never gets overflow:hidden, which would also clip its own drop shadow.

rules.name: The Soft-by-Design Rule
rules.body: Shadows stay low-opacity on purpose. Deepening a shadow to create emphasis is the wrong lever — reach for type weight and spacing first.

dos: Do pull every color, size, radius, shadow, duration, and spring config from src/theme/tokens.ts — no exceptions, no inline hex or magic numbers.
Do give every primary Button and domain-aware pill an explicit domain prop matching the screen's content rather than relying on the 'progress' default.
Do give every tappable element a visible pressed state, a minimum 44pt touch size, and an accessibilityRole.
Do use the springy, bouncy press feel everywhere — it's the deliberate default feel, not a bug to tone down.
Do keep the mascot's encouraging/celebrating poses as the sole reservoir of exclamation marks and hype language; everywhere else, copy stays sober.
Do name colors and describe components by what they mean in this system, not by generic Material role names.
donts: Don't reach for accentRed/accentRedDeep/accentRedSoft in new or touched code — they're a transitional shim, use the domain tokens directly.
Don't mix two domain colors as accents on one screen without a specific reason.
Don't use fontWeight anywhere, or pair fontFamily with fontWeight — weight lives in which Fredoka cut is loaded.
Don't let this system drift toward flat generic SaaS — no thin-bordered flat cards, no blue-violet gradients, no interchangeable 'professional tool' look.
Don't deepen a shadow to create emphasis — shadows stay soft and low-opacity by design.
Don't place the mascot in an error state, or give the encouraging pose any hint of mockery, sadness, or apology.
